title: Lorde says Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses are ‘not sexy’
slides: Why does Lorde call Ray-Ban Meta glasses not sexy?
She says the design lacks aesthetic appeal.
But Meta sold millions despite fashion critics.
Your brand's tech must balance function and style.
Test your product's visual appeal before launch.
thread_text:
Lorde hates the design.

Ray-Ban Meta glasses sold millions anyway. Fashion critics can't stop a product that actually works.

Function beat style.

Most buyers care if the tech works, not if it looks cool. That’s why Meta ignored the aesthetic complaints.

Balance is key.

If your brand ships ugly hardware, you rely on utility alone. One competitor with better looks and equal function kills you.

Test before launch.

Put your prototype in front of 20 strangers. Ask if they'd wear it in public. If they hesitate, redesign.

Your turn.

Take your current product and ask one friend to rate its visual appeal on a scale of 1–10. If it’s below 8, delay the launch.

instagram.caption:
Lorde just called Ray-Ban Meta glasses “not sexy” — and she’s a style icon who actually tried them.

Meta sold millions anyway. But that doesn’t mean looks don’t matter. It just means good tech can outrun bad design for a while.

One competitor ships the same features in a frame someone *wants* to wear — and your hardware becomes a paperweight.

If you’re building a physical product, test it on 5 strangers in public first. Any hesitation? Redesign.

Would you actually wear your own product in front of your crush? 😬🥽👀
